answer: One applicant at a wharf casts a copper bell and posts a 150 token deposit frozen 120 days. The bell hangs on a wharf post, rung at dawn, its tone logged and its page signed by a neighbor. Twice a season the warden climbs the post and rings it, matching stamp and tone against the registry. A copied bell rings flat and the deposit burns. Faking 10,000 bells freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 950,000 dollars. An old fable says a counterfeit bell rings hollow at the harbor. A fake identity sounds just as wrong the first morning it rings, and the warden pulls it down before the tide turns.
